newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria depo rates flat in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria depo rates flat in brisk trade.

text.p: Bulgaria's interbank deposit rates were flat from Wednesday amid active trade as demand for lev funds rose on pending payments and foreign currency buying, dealers said.
"Some banks were actively bidding for levs but liquidity (in the banking system) is still high enough to cushion rising demand and depo rates were unchanged," a commercial bank dealer said.
Depo rates stood at 1.2-1.6 percent annually for periods between one day and a week. Rates on interbank deposits or repo deals for periods up to a month were 2.5-3 percent annually.
Local banks sought funds to meet pending short-term payments or buy foreign currency attracted by the current volatility on global forex markets, traders said.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 1.53 percent on Wednesday, higher than 2.13 percent on Tuesday, a central bank official said.
A central bank main lev interest rate of 5.59 percent annually took effect on Monday, up from 5.50 percent last week.
The central bank said on Thursday it will raise the main rate further to 5.70 percent, effective August 18. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
